notes.rule: His word 2026-11-25: edits need not be public domain; anything Orthodox or of Christ, Western art too, nothing heretical. None held in Greece or Italy (lib/marketing/heritagePictures.ts): New York and Saint Petersburg.
fetched_not_used: The Russian Museum's Nativity, early 16th century (DRZh-1248), 9168 by 12000: the first plan's night, replaced by El Greco at his word that Western art may be used
The Tretyakov's Our Lady of Vladimir (my.tretyakov.ru 9256), 1457 by 2048: too small for the drop's close shots

For the three full-style versions (2026-11-25), fetched from The Met and not used: Rembrandt's Adoration with the Lamp (373069; its open line work reads as a drawing, not a night), Christ at Emmaus: the Larger Plate (391998; a glory of beams behind Him), Christ Preaching (371733), Christ Presented to the People (343142; too small for close shots), La Tour's Penitent Magdalen (436839; the Western reading of the Magdalen, which the Orthodox Church does not share), and engravings whose halos are beams (Raimondi 342532 and 342564, Dürer 391267, Rembrandt 391684, Goltzius 398389, Lucas van Leyden 364759, Matham 338386), or too small, too faint or a crowd (Schongauer 367002 and 336162, Rembrandt 334647, 373921, 391023 and 391993, Dürer 388800, 391052, 391240 and 360355, Zoboli 340995, Cigoli 338521, Annibale Carracci 341351, Reni 340615, the Master of Jesus in Bethlehem 337757, Mellan 391939)
